### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9bab3118bd305eba9db69ff10672cc7d5e9d8d5f` — the merge of head `fe109ec6cf2eee4c8d64316174270301ce7d9fc6` into base `d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9bab3118bd305eba9db69ff10672cc7d5e9d8d5f && git checkout 9bab3118bd305eba9db69ff10672cc7d5e9d8d5f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73 fe109ec6cf2eee4c8d64316174270301ce7d9fc6 && git checkout -B drift-repro d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73 && git merge --no-ff fe109ec6cf2eee4c8d64316174270301ce7d9fc6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d1ebe86dd3c2ec380de7c2c8607306c8e4bb9b73` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-A) at head `fe109ec6cf2eee4c8d64316174270301ce7d9fc6`, read 2026-11-20T07:34Z. No L2 is owed: the change declares `Clause-②: no` with no narrowing arm, touches no `packages/spec/src/**`, and changes no governed rule text.

### Shape and declarations

- Draft, base `main`. 4 commits: a fix, a main merge, the attribution fix, and the census regeneration. 8 files, +127/−10.
- `Fixes #35440` is the only closing keyword, and the card's "Done when" is met:
  - the ledger note and the docs name `user.admin_removed_pending`;
  - ban and unban write a row, pinned in the shared harness (`pending-sso-users.test.ts`), with an ablation.
- The claim amendment 7031864853 adds `user-ban-write.ts` to the file surface before the commit that edits it.
- **`Clause-②: no` holds.**
  - The audit rows and the mirror row's attribution are audit-trail behaviour, not a widened accept set.
  - The one widened type is the exported `AdminAuditDecisions` union, which gains one `event` member. It is a write-side tag that `writeAdminAudit` stamps. #35422 added `user.admin_removed_pending` the same way under `Clause-②: no` (my L1 7004734980), and this follows that precedent.
  - No request body, route or response shape moves.

### Code

- **`auditBan`** runs only after the committed write:
  - for a ban, after `applyUserBan` and `deleteUserSessions`;
  - for an unban, after `applyUserUnban`.

  Every refusal returns before it: host refusal, last-administrator 400, unknown user. It goes through the siblings' `writeAdminAudit`, which writes under `SYSTEM_CTX` and steps aside when there is no engine or no `sys_audit_log`. A failure there is logged and does not fail the answer, so the door's status is unchanged. `hostNotified` is `host?.notified === true`, so with no host wired it is `false`.
- **`engineUserBanWriter`.** `authSystemWriteContext()` returns `isSystem: true` unconditionally; attribution is the additive half, as its docblock says. Spreading it after `positions: []` and `permissions: []` keeps the authorization the literal context had, so the last-administrator guard still judges the write. On the admin-plugin path, the vendor `internalAdapter` already wrote through the attribution seam. The two writers now agree.
- **Census shard.** `docs/audits/…/plugin-auth.md` moves one site from "elevated" to "elevation undecidable" (42→41, 45→46). That is the census reading a spread context, not a change in elevation; the dev also tried a literal spelling, and the census still read it as undecidable. It is generated and non-governed. It overlaps #34738 only in this shard, so whichever PR lands second reruns `tenant-audit-census --write`.

### Tests and controls

- **Pins:**
  - Plugin off and on: one `update` row per committed change, naming the admin as `user_id` / `actor` on the target `sys_user`, with the exact `metadata`.
  - The ban-column write's context carries `isSystem: true` and `attributedUserId` = admin on both writers.
  - No host: `hostNotified: false`.
  - CONTROL: a host-refused ban (409), a self-ban (400) and a host-refused unban (403) write no row. Its ban half still writes exactly one.
- **Ablations:**
  - Deleting the `auditBan` call turned the describe 4/4 red.
  - Swapping the bare `{ isSystem: true, … }` context back in turned the attribution pin red for plugin off. That is the case that moved, because the admin-plugin writer was already attributed.
  - Both were restored blob-equal.

### Prose, sentence by sentence

- **Changeset.** Each sentence checks out against the code:
  - both doors write one row on a committed change, through the shared writer;
  - `action: 'update'` on the target `sys_user`, naming the administrator, with `metadata` `{ event, hostNotified }`;
  - a refused one writes none;
  - with the admin plugin off, the ban-column write is attributed, so the mirror row names the administrator, and the written fields are unchanged;
  - reason and expiry stay on the mirror row;
  - the ledger note and the docs name `user.admin_removed_pending`.
- **`authentication.mdx`.** The remove-sso-user sentence (`action: 'delete'`, `{ event: 'user.admin_removed_pending', hostNotified }`, none on a refusal) matches `pending-sso-users.ts:878`. The ban/unban sentence matches the code above.
- **Ledger note.** "a removal that committed writes one admin audit row (sys_audit_log action delete, metadata event user.admin_removed_pending with hostNotified), a refused one none" is true and carries no tracker id.
- **Endpoint header** (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts`). "plugin-audit's mirror row … names the administrator on both writers … but carries neither the event nor `hostNotified`, so it does not stand in for this row" is true, and it is why the row is not redundant.

### Your three points

1. **The PR body predates the patch round.** No rewrite is owed for L1. The delta and its readings are in the PR comment and in dev report 7032908183, and this ACCEPT records what the body omits: the `engineUserBanWriter` attribution change, the census shard, and ablation 2. If the landing commit message is built from the body, have the seat take these three lines into it. A body patch that pushes the attribution header off the top would cost more than it adds.
2. **The census shard.** Accepted, as above.
3. **No ledger notes on the ban doors.** Accepted. `admin/ban-user` and `admin/unban-user` sit in the vendor route list (`auth-route-ledger.ts:429`, `:443`) with no `note` field to amend. The endpoint header and the docs are where those doors are described.

### Nit (not owed)

The changeset opens on `Clause-②: no` with no subject line. Six pending changesets on `main` do the same, so it is not a defect, but most open with a `fix(scope): …` line, which reads better as the CHANGELOG entry's head.

### Gates and routing

- CI at `fe109ec6`: 55 check runs, 40 `success` and 15 `skipped`, none red.
- Local readings: 104/104 derived families exit 0 at the head, and the plugin-auth suite passes 287 files.
- This PR is not governed, so d7-A lands it under `landing-operations.md` after `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35758` reads clean. Rerun `overlap-check` against #34738 at landing.
